channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: 16th Annual International Juried Exhibition · Gallery 110
item.description: Gallery 110's annual juried exhibition, running since 2011, invites emerging and established artists worldwide to submit original work in any two- or three-dimensional medium — photography included — for a show in the gallery's Pioneer Square space from 4 to 27 February 2027. The 2026 juror is Ryan Hardesty, Executive Director of the Jordan Schnitzer Museum of Art at Washington State University, who spent twelve years at the Northwest Museum of Arts & Culture in Spokane and has held positions at the Institute of Contemporary Art in Boston, the Rose Art Museum at Brandeis and the Fogg Art Museum at Harvard. Hardesty has chosen an open call with no set theme. He awards first, second and third prizes of $1,000, $500 and $300, and there is a $200 People's Choice award. Gallery 110 is an artist-run 501(c)(3) non-profit supported by 4Culture and the City of Seattle Office of Arts & Culture; accepted artists get professional reviews and inclusion in the monthly First Thursday Art Walk, which draws over a thousand visitors. Applications are accepted from 21 July to 31 October 2026. Finalists are notified by email and phone in December 2026 and are responsible for delivery and prepaid return shipping. Open to artists 18 and over. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: $40 (3 images) + $10 each addl, up to 10. Prize: $1,000 / $500 / $300 + $200 People's Choice.

item.title: Call for Entries 2027 · ROY G BIV Gallery
item.description: ROY G BIV Gallery for Emerging Artists in Columbus, Ohio runs its exhibition programme from one annual call for entries, and this is the round for the 2027 season. Selected artists are given a month-long small group exhibition during the 2027 calendar year, curated by the gallery director. Submissions come from artists local and global and are reviewed and voted on by a panel of jurors from the contemporary arts community; the 2027 jurors are filmmaker and visual artist Yusef Ferguson, a 2025 Greater Columbus Arts Council Visual Arts Fellow currently exhibiting at the Columbus Museum of Art, and sculptor Dana Lynn Harper, who holds an MFA from Penn State and makes ritual votive works about racial identity and cultural heritage. ROY defines emerging artists as those early in their careers, not represented by a gallery, and not yet substantially celebrated by the media, funding circles or the public; artists who have shown at ROY before are ineligible apart from ImageOHIO and the annual small works member show. Entry requires a ROY G BIV membership costing $25 for the calendar year. Submissions go by email with up to 10 images (JPG or PNG, under 1.5 MB each) or up to 5 video URLs, plus an artist statement, CV and list of works. Two-dimensional work must arrive ready to hang, and artists are responsible for transport and installation. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: $25 membership. Prize: None listed.

item.title: RAA&M National Juried Show 2026 · Rockport Art Association & Museum
item.description: The Rockport Art Association & Museum's annual national juried exhibition hangs in the Aldro T. Hibbard and Maddocks galleries on Cape Ann from 14 November to 31 December 2026, with a gala and awards reception on 13 November. Photography is one of the named media categories, alongside painting, drawing, mixed media, collage, original printmaking and sculpture. Over $25,000 in cash and merchandise awards is on offer, including a $5,000 Grand Prize. Garin Baker is juror of selection and of awards. Artists may submit up to four works but only one will be selected if accepted; the maximum size is 36 inches on the longest side plus a reasonable frame. Membership is not required to enter. The museum takes a 40% commission on sales from the exhibition. Work made in an instructional setting, including workshops and classes, is not eligible, and accepted work must stay hanging until the show closes unless sold. The AI policy is unusually specific for a photography entrant: no artificial intelligence may be used in the conception or development of the work, images must originate with the artist through a light capture process, and no synthetic images, stock imagery, replacement skies or generative fill are permitted. Editing is allowed as long as every component belongs to the artist. Results appear in the OnlineJuriedShows artist profile on 25 September 2026. — Deadline: September 7, 2026. Fee: $50 first entry ($40 members) + $10 each addl. Prize: $25,000+ in awards ($5,000 Grand Prize).

item.title: DeHaan Artist of Distinction Award 2026 — Round 2 · Indy Arts Council
item.description: Funded entirely by a legacy gift from the Christel DeHaan Family Foundation and administered by the Indy Arts Council, the DeHaan Artist of Distinction Award honours up to five contemporary visual artists a year with project grants of up to $10,000 each. Photography is named in the list of eligible art forms alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, textiles and digital or new media. The programme is built for risk: it funds aspirational, innovative projects that push an artist's practice in new directions, and applicants are asked to make the case that their work brings something new to the field. Applicants must have lived or worked in Indiana for at least three consecutive years at the date of application, must remain in the state for a year after the award activities conclude, must show five years of documented experience through solo exhibitions, national exposure, critical reviews, residencies, fellowships or juried shows, and must have generated consistent income from their work in visual art. Projects must conclude within twelve months of the signed agreement, and awardees take part in a professionally curated group exhibition at Gallery 924 at the Indy Arts Council and submit a final report documenting the project's impact. There are two rounds a year; Round 1 closed on 3 May 2026 and Round 2 closes on 18 October 2026. Applications are free and go through the council's grant platform, and alternative formats such as dictated or video responses can be arranged. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to 5 × $10,000.

item.title: 16th Annual National Juried Exhibition · Marshall University Art Galleries
item.description: Marshall University's School of Art & Design invites artists to its 16th Annual National Juried Exhibition, shown in the Charles W. and Norma C. Carroll Gallery in the Visual Arts Center in Huntington, West Virginia from 18 January to 25 February 2027, with an awards reception on 18 February. Artists may submit up to three works in any medium, so photography and lens-based work are eligible. The juror is Rachel Rearick, Executive Director of Contemporary Craft and an adjunct faculty member at Carnegie Mellon University teaching museum operations and public art; she is an artist member of the Associated Artists of Pittsburgh and the Pittsburgh Print Group. Entrants must be 18 or over and hold permanent residence in the United States, with exceptions for students and military personnel holding US resident status; work previously shown in a Marshall University gallery will not be considered. Entry is $30 for up to three works, or $15 for current Marshall students with ID, and everything is handled through the entry form on the gallery's own site. Jurying runs 3 to 14 November 2026 with email notifications on 18 November, and accepted work must reach the gallery between 7 and 11 December. All accepted pieces must arrive display-ready, and artists cover delivery and insurance in transit. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: $30 (up to 3 entries; $15 Marshall students). Prize: None listed.

item.title: Artist-in-Residence — January–May 2027 · Surel's Place
item.description: A month-long live-work residency in Garden City, Idaho, in the house built by the late artist Surel Mitchell. The residency is free to apply to and free to hold: rent, utilities and wi-fi are covered, and residents receive a $100-per-week living stipend, a $300 travel stipend, use of the house bicycles, free or discounted tickets to local art events, marketing through the organisation's channels, and logistics and installation help for their public events. Each resident is assigned a host who introduces them to the local arts community. The programme is open to professional visual, literary and performance artists — the org describes it as "any artist who needs a place to focus" — though the property cannot accommodate loud or messy processes such as welding or blacksmithing, and work that is predominantly conceptual may find less enthusiasm with the jury. Residents must live at the house for the residency (no studio-only stays), take no other employment during it, give at least one public workshop of two to three hours, present a show or lecture on the residency work, and donate one piece to Surel's Place for future fundraising. The commission on sales arising from the residency is 35%. Applicants must be 25 or older and non-smokers; partners may join but children and pets cannot. This September 1 deadline covers residencies running January to May 2027; applications for playwrights and screenwriters are paused until the March 2027 round. Visual artists apply by email with a cover letter, a proposal including a workshop outline, a CV, and 4 to 6 images with an image list. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 1-month residency + stipends.

item.title: 1858 Prize for Contemporary Southern Art 2026 · Gibbes Museum of Art
item.description: An annual award from the Gibbes Museum of Art and its Society 1858 auxiliary, given to an artist whose work contributes to a new understanding of art in the South. The prize welcomes applications from artists working across any media, and photography has a long history here — past winners and finalists include Sally Mann, William Christenberry, Deborah Luster, Birney Imes, Stephen Marc, Jeff Whetstone, Susan Worsham, Jennifer Shaw and 2025 finalist Tommy Kha. Alongside the monetary award, a work chosen by the Gibbes curatorial team in collaboration with the artist goes on display in the museum's Mary Jackson Modern and Contemporary Galleries for the year following the announcement. Previous winners have gone on to Joan Mitchell Fellowships, Guggenheim Memorial Foundation awards and Pollock-Krasner grants, with work entering the collections of the National Gallery of Art, the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Art Institute of Chicago. Eligibility is geographic rather than medium-based: artists must reside in, work in, or be from Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, West Virginia or the District of Columbia. Applications go through SlideRoom with a registration form, an artist statement of 150 words or less, a CV, and a portfolio of up to ten images or videos of recent original work at 300dpi or better. Submissions are reviewed by a panel of visual arts professionals, Society 1858 representatives and Gibbes staff; the winner and finalists are notified in October 2026, with a public announcement later in the year. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Berlendis Venice Art Prize 2027 · Marignana Arte
item.description: The second edition of a Venice prize run by Kosmos Contemporary Venice APS with Marignana Arte, on the theme "Have We Crossed the Threshold? A Journey Beyond Borders, Identities and Languages" — crossing as an aesthetic, political and existential practice. Photography is explicitly named among the eligible media, alongside painting, drawing, printmaking and graphic arts, collage, sculpture and installation, textile art and video art. A jury of eight selects twenty finalists, ten in an Emergent section for artists aged 18 to 30 and ten in a Contemporary section for artists over 30, who show together at Spazio Berlendis — a 300-square-metre former boatyard carpentry workshop in Cannaregio that has hosted the Gwangju Biennale and currently houses the Grenada and Guatemala pavilions of the 2026 Biennale Arte. The finalists' exhibition runs 20 February to 21 March 2027 with a dedicated publication, and every finalist receives a free copy. Cash prizes are €1,000 gross to the Emergent winner and €2,500 gross to the Contemporary winner, with withholding tax of 25% for Italian residents and 30% for others. Five further special prizes offer exhibitions: two solo shows at Marignana Project in 2027 (one per section), a group show at Fondazione THE BANK ETS in Bassano del Grappa, a solo or group show at Galleria Alessandro Casciaro in Bolzano or Venice, and a solo or group show at Spazio Magazzino. Each artist submits one work, up to 200×200cm for two-dimensional pieces and 20kg maximum, with a 4-to-10-page PDF portfolio and one to three images. Works remain the property of the artists, but shipping both ways, customs and insurance are at the artist's expense. Finalists are announced by 10 December 2026. — Deadline: September 24, 2026. Fee: €25 (18–30) / €35 (over 30). Prize: €2,500 + €1,000 + 5 exhibition prizes.

item.title: Foundwork Artist Prize 2026
item.description: An annual juried award recognising outstanding emerging and mid-career artists working in any media. The honoree receives an unrestricted $10,000 grant, a studio visit with each of the five jurors, and an interview for Foundwork's Dialogues programme; three further artists are named to a Short List and each receives a $1,000 micro-grant. The 2026 jury is Stefan Benchoam (artist and co-founder of Proyectos Ultravioleta and NuMu, Guatemala City), François Ghebaly (founder of the Los Angeles and New York gallery), Manuela Moscoso (director of the Center for Art, Research and Alliances and curator of Ecuador's 2026 Venice pavilion), Gabi Ngcobo (director of Kunstinstituut Melly, Rotterdam, and curator of the 10th Berlin Biennale) and Esther Schipper (founder of the Berlin gallery). Photography is well represented: the 2025 honoree Antonia Kuo works with photochemical painting on silver gelatin paper, and photographer Clifford Prince King was on the 2023 Short List. There is no separate entry fee, but applicants must hold an active Foundwork artist membership — $6 a month, with a 30-day free trial for new members — and keep a published profile carrying at least six artworks and an artist statement throughout the selection period, which runs from 5pm PT on 25 September 2026 to 5pm PT on 31 December 2026. Staff shortlist fifty finalists for the jury, who pick one honoree and three Short List artists. Open worldwide to artists 18 and over, except residents of Argentina, Arizona, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Cuba, Iran, Kosovo, Latvia, Macedonia, North Korea, Quebec, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Serbia, Sudan, Syria and the UAE. Past honorees cannot win again, and past Short List artists must wait three years. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: Free (membership $6/month required). Prize: $10,000 + 3 × $1,000.

item.title: Hornsby Art Prize 2026 · Hornsby Shire Council
item.description: Established in 2009 and run by Hornsby Shire Council with the Hornsby Art Society, this non-acquisitive prize celebrates Australian contemporary art across five categories — Painting, Drawing, Printmaking, Photography and Sculpture — each carrying its own $1,500 award, so photographers compete for a dedicated Photography Award as well as the $10,000 major prize. The overall pool is $23,000, which also covers a $5,000 Hornsby Shire Local Artist Award and a $500 People's Choice. There is no set theme. Artists may enter up to two works; 2D pieces are capped at 125cm in height and width including the frame, and nothing may exceed 15kg. Finalist works must not have appeared in any other art prize exhibition and must be for sale, with a 20% commission going to the Hornsby Art Society. Finalists are announced by 5pm on 1 September and the exhibition runs at Wallarobba Arts and Cultural Centre from 16 October to 1 November 2026, with the prize announced on opening day. — Deadline: August 20, 2026. Fee: AU$40 per entry. Prize: AU$10,000 + AU$1,500 Photography Award.

item.title: Kangaroo Valley Art Prize 2026 · Visual Arts in the Valley
item.description: The headline prize of the Visual Arts in the Valley festival, held in the Kangaroo Valley Hall and venues around the valley in the NSW Southern Highlands. The terms of entry are deliberately wide: any original work of visual art by an Australian artist or an artist residing in Australia is eligible, expressly including photographic art, digital art, new media and video alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, textiles and collage. Work must have been made within two years of the closing date and must not have been shown by Visual Arts in the Valley before; maximum hung size is 115cm wide by 180cm high including the frame. Alongside the $10,000 main prize there is a $3,000 Highly Commended, a $2,000 Commended, a $4,000 Young & Emerging Art Prize for artists aged 30 or under (with a $1,000 Commended), a $1,500 Salon of Local Artists Prize, a $1,000 People's Choice and a $500 Packing Room Prize. Judged by painter Steven Harvey, senior lecturer at the National Art School, with Olivia Welch of Ngununggula Regional Gallery curating. The exhibition runs 2–5 October 2026. — Deadline: August 21, 2026. Fee: AU$30 per work (AU$80 for three). Prize: AU$10,000 + AU$4,000 Young & Emerging.

item.title: The Ingram Prize 2026 · The Ingram Collection
item.description: An annual purchase prize for artists within five years of graduating from a UK-based art school, run by The Ingram Collection — one of the largest publicly accessible collections of modern and contemporary British art. Entry is free, any medium is accepted, there is no size restriction, and artists may submit up to two works. Three artists receive the Ingram Prize and have their work acquired for the Collection; a fourth work is chosen personally by founder Chris Ingram for the Founder's Award; and one prizewinner is given a solo exhibition at Lightbox Gallery, Woking, in 2027. Shortlisted work is shown at Unit 1 Gallery | Workshop in London from 5 to 11 November 2026, with the winners announced at the opening event on 4 November. Eligible applicants are those aged 18 or over holding a practice-based visual arts qualification from a UK institution completed between 1 April 2021 and 31 October 2026. — Deadline: August 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Acquisition + solo exhibition.

item.title: NEW WORK 2027 — We Come in Pieces · Prospect Art
item.description: Prospect Art's annual NEW WORK commission is a $1,500 project grant funding a new, conceptually driven work made in response to a curatorial theme — for 2027, 'We Come in Pieces', developed by Curatorial Fellow Alma Sammel. The theme proposes the Alien not as an Other but as a method of estrangement, and asks for work that displaces the point of listening, seeing or sensing: speculative cosmologies, ecological systems, satellites and orbital debris, fungal networks, oceans, algorithmic intelligences. Research-based practice is especially encouraged. Photography is named among the welcomed media alongside moving image, installation, sculpture, performance, sound, digital media and social practice. A single application also puts artists in consideration for ONE WORK, an online series built around a single completed artwork, and BROADCAST, a curated programme of screenings and artist talks that pays a $125 speaking fee. Applications ask for a 250-word project description, a sketch or mock-up, three links to finished works, a 200-word statement on the theme, a bio and exhibition history, and a budget. The $10 administrative fee is waived on request by email, no explanation needed. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: $10 (waiver on request). Prize: $1,500 commission.

item.title: Heysen Prize for Landscape 2026 · Hahndorf Academy
item.description: A biennial contemporary art prize established in 1997 to commemorate Sir Hans Heysen, run by the Hahndorf Academy in the Adelaide Hills. The 2026 edition asks artists to express their connection with — or concern for — protecting the Australian environment, taking Heysen's own record as an early environmental activist as its starting point. 'Landscape' is defined broadly to include every aspect of the natural, rural and urban landscape, and the prize is open to 2D, 3D and moving-image work; photographers have been regular finalists, and past selections include Che Chorley and Mark Kimber. The main prize of $15,000 is acquisitive; a non-acquisitive People's Choice Prize of $1,000 is also awarded. Finalists are notified on 31 August 2026 and deliver work to Hahndorf between 7 and 23 September; the finalist exhibition runs 10 October to 6 December 2026, opening with a launch on 10 October at which the winners are announced. — Deadline: August 21, 2026. Fee: AU$55. Prize: AU$15,000 acquisitive.

item.title: Windgate Artist in Residence — Fall 2027 & Spring 2028 · UA Little Rock School of Art and Design
item.description: A semester-long funded residency at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock, supported by the Windgate Foundation and open to artists, designers and craftspeople in any medium. The selected artist receives a $30,000 stipend for the semester, housing, a $2,000 materials and travel budget, and 24-hour access to a private studio plus the Windgate Center's specialist facilities — a photography studio, printmaking studio, woodshop with CNC and laser cutter, ceramics, jewellery and metalsmithing studios, and a smithy and foundry. Residents are not required to teach courses; the commitments are weekly open studio hours, two public artist talks (one at the Windgate Center, one at the Arkansas Museum of Fine Arts), one two-day student workshop, BFA critiques and up to two guest class sessions, plus donating one work to the university's permanent collection. Two terms are open: Fall 2027 (15 August to 15 December) and Spring 2028 (15 January to 15 May), each with its own application. Applicants need an active practice, evidence of exhibiting nationally or internationally, experience working with students, and a degree, certificate or equivalent experience; international artists must already hold visa authorisation covering the residency, as the university cannot sponsor visas. Applications go through Workday with a cover letter, CV, three references and a portfolio of up to 20 images. — Deadline: August 23, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $30,000 stipend + housing.

item.title: Create! Magazine Issue #60 — The Artist's World
item.description: Open call for Issue No. 60 of Create! Magazine, an artist-led print and digital publication for contemporary art. The theme, The Artist's World, asks what it means to build a world as an artist — a universe made through the work, an independent practice that makes its own opportunities, or simply inhabiting the planet; the brief is open to all interpretations and all subjects and media are welcome, photography among them. Juried by Marina Granger, founder of the New York advisory The Artist Advisory, former guest curator of the magazine's 2024 Women's Print Issue and curator of Lunation at Warnes Contemporary and The Feminine Divine at Kaliner Gallery. Selected artists receive a four-page spread in the print and digital editions, website and social features, and a complimentary digital issue. Submit up to 10 works (cohesive bodies and series encouraged) with a 300-word bio and artist statement; $35 covers three images. Open to artists worldwide with no academic background required, and there are no further fees if published. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $35 / 3 images. Prize: Publication.

item.title: XIV «Galicia» Award of Contemporary Photography · Outono Fotográfico
item.description: The fourteenth edition of the Premio «Galicia» de Fotografía Contemporánea, founded in 2013 within the International Outono Fotográfico Festival and run by the Asociación OF. Outono Fotográfico with the Xunta de Galicia, the Deputación de Lugo and the University of Vigo's Ourense campus. It seeks complete photographic projects on a free theme, judged above all on how they sit within the discourse of contemporary photography, and is open to any author working with photography or the photographic regardless of nationality. Two awards are made from the same pool of entries. The Jury Prize produces an exhibition of the winning project with a curator appointed by the association, opening in Lugo and touring Galicia and Portugal for two years before the exhibition becomes the artist's property, plus a book in the "Galicia Contemporary Photography Prize" series from Difusora de Letras, Artes e Ideas, distributed in bookshops with a percentage of the print run to the author. The Organisation Prize produces a comparable exhibition at the Alterarte Gallery on the Ourense campus with an accompanying booklet. Projects must have been made between October 2016 and October 2026 and must not have been fully funded by another competition or published in full. Submit up to 15 images (minimum 3,000 px on the long side) with a synopsis of up to 2,500 characters and a 1,500-character biography. Entry costs €22 per project. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: €22 per project. Prize: Touring exhibition + book.

item.title: Nocturne: Photography After Dark · TCG Gallery
item.description: International juried online exhibition on the night — what becomes visible once daylight recedes and darkness, limited visibility and artificial light reshape the world. Streetlights isolating gestures, windows glowing against dark buildings, long exposures stretching time, flash revealing what the eye would miss; beyond the city, moonlight, stars, weather and deep shadow remaking the landscape. Urban night photography, nocturnal landscapes, astrophotography, nightlife, interiors, staged scenes, low-light portraits, light painting and experimental work are all welcome, with night read as a physical setting, a psychological condition or simply a space where ordinary life behaves differently. Digital, film, alternative process, documentary, fine art, conceptual and mixed-media photographic work accepted. Blind review wherever possible, with emphasis on the work rather than biography or exhibition history; approximately 30 images are selected for the curated online exhibition and permanent website archive, running 1–21 November 2026. Fee waivers are offered on the honour system for artists experiencing financial hardship. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $15 (up to 3 images); fee waivers available. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Outdoor Photography Magazine — Environmental Wildlife
item.description: Submit up to 5 images on the theme of environmental wildlife — animals shown in the context of the landscape they live in — for the 'One Thing This Month' reader competition (OP 333) in Outdoor Photography Magazine (UK). The winner receives a Cumulus Moonrain Jacket (RRP £325). Entries need captions of up to 75 words covering where, why and how each image was taken, plus full technical details in the magazine's stated order (camera and lens, focal length, ISO, shutter speed, aperture, tripod or handheld). Free to enter, uploaded in bulk through the magazine's Google Form. The magazine publishes work taken outside in the landscape, wildlife, nature, adventure and travel genres, and asks that images be made ethically and with sensitivity to environmental and conservation issues. — Deadline: October 5, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Cumulus Moonrain Jacket (£325) + Publication.

item.title: SELF PORTRAIT Photography Exhibit · Decode Gallery
item.description: Decode Gallery invites photographers worldwide to submit their best self portrait work for a themed gallery show in Tucson, Arizona. The gallery frames self portraiture as an exploration of identity and an intimate glimpse into the life of the artist, and is looking for work that reveals a story rather than simply records a likeness. At least twenty-six images are selected by juror Holly Hart, a conceptual fine art photographer who founded Decode Gallery after a BA in Photography from the Art Institute of Seattle. Selected photographers pay nothing further: the gallery handles all printing itself on an Epson printer with Epson Ultra Premium Luster paper, and presents work in museum-quality 22 x 22 inch white frames with precut white mats in a range of sizes. Submitted files are never cropped, only scaled for the best fit in the mat. One print is made per accepted image and archived in a flat file for two years after the show. Entry is $40 for up to five photographs, open to amateurs and professionals alike. Photographers are notified by email within two weeks of the deadline and high-resolution files are due two days later. The exhibition runs November 7 to 28, 2026, opening on November 7. Work may optionally be listed for sale, with the gallery taking a 50 per cent commission and all rights to the file and print remaining with the photographer. — Deadline: September 18, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: HUMOROUS: The Art of Laughter · Armory Art Center
item.description: The Armory Art Center's juried gallery exhibition for Florida-based artists, hung alongside the tenth annual Creative Market on its historic West Palm Beach campus in Howard Park. The theme is humour in all its registers: playful portraiture and caricature, visual puns and wordplay, absurd and surreal scenes, comics and graphic narratives, everyday life with a twist, pop-culture and nostalgia parody, and animal antics. The Armory argues that humour in art does more than amuse, that it shifts perspectives, crosses language and cultural lines, and gives satire a way to critique politics and social norms. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside oil, acrylic, water media, pastel, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, sculpture, fibre, wood, ceramics and digital art; AI-generated work is not accepted, and diptychs and triptychs must be uploaded as a single image. Entry is $43 plus processing for up to two pieces, each judged individually, so the jury may take neither, one or both. The show is curated and juried by Armory staff with an anonymous juror, and first, second and third awards are given. Open to amateur and professional artists eighteen and over living in Florida. Notification is by October 16 and the exhibition runs November 2 to December 26, 2026 with a reception on November 19. All work must be for sale, with a 60/40 split in the artist's favour, and artists cover shipping both ways. — Deadline: October 4, 2026. Fee: $43 (up to 2 works). Prize: Awards + Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Exhibition Proposals · Falkirk Cultural Center
item.description: The City of San Rafael invites artists, groups and organisations to propose exhibitions for the 2027 calendar at two civic venues: Falkirk Cultural Center, an 1888 Queen Anne mansion on the National Historic Register whose three second-floor rooms have shown art since the City took it on in 1974, and the recently renovated San Rafael Downtown Library, one of California's Carnegie libraries, open again after a restoration that preserved the 1909 building. Falkirk hosts five or six exhibits a year, each running roughly six weeks, with most openings timed to the Downtown San Rafael Second Friday Art Walk. Proposals are judged on community interest, quality of work and a track record of achievement, and applicants are asked to show they can curate an exhibit large enough to fill one gallery room at Falkirk or the Library's display shelves, which are built for three-dimensional work. There is no medium restriction and no residency requirement stated. Proposals go first to City staff, then to the Public Art Review Board in October, and selected proposals move into a contract. Exhibitors handle their own transport, installation, take-down, title cards and opening reception, and provide images good enough for the City to build a virtual version of the show for accessibility; the City provides staffing during open hours, show cards and promotion. Sales run through the City on a 70/30 split in the artist's favour. Application is $5 through CaFE. — Deadline: September 27, 2026. Fee: $5. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Art at Emerson Hall: An Emerging Artist Community Showcase
item.description: Emerson Hall was built in 1870 as a Universalist church and named for Ralph Waldo Emerson; it is a rare surviving example of English Country Gothic architecture, with stained glass, a curving loft and an exposed-beam cathedral ceiling, sitting on the National Register of Historic Places at the corner of Forest and Bedford Streets in downtown Stamford. The Emerson Hall Foundation, incorporated in 2023 to keep the building working as a venue for artists, musicians and educators, is filling it for three days with the work of eight to ten local emerging artists. The organisers are explicit about who they want: artists with little to no prior exhibition experience — "If you've never had a 'real' show before, this is your moment." Painting, drawing, sculpture, photography, textiles and jewellery are all accepted for review. Applicants must be based in the Greater Stamford area and be 16 or older, with parent or guardian permission required under 18. There is no entry fee and applications close 15 August 2026. Work is chosen by a four-person selection committee of Stamford-area artists and educators, and the programme is presented with the Unitarian Universalist Congregation in Stamford with support from a City of Stamford Arts & Culture Commission grant. — Deadline: August 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Between Here and There · Greenwich Art Society
item.description: The Greenwich Art Society's annual member exhibition is juried this year by Antonia Pocock, a curatorial assistant at the Whitney Museum of American Art, who organised Claes Oldenburg: Drawn from Life and has written for Art in America, Texte zur Kunst and Nka. The theme is the space between where we were, where we are and where we are going — physical, emotional, personal or imagined — and the society invites work reading it as movement, memory, transformation, discovery or simply a moment of pause. Photography is a named category alongside painting, drawing, pastel, watercolour, sculpture, original digital art, fibre arts, traditional printmaking, mixed media and collage; digital prints of original art and AI-generated work are excluded, and entrants confirm the work is their own and not AI-generated. Work must have been completed in 2023 or later and must not have been shown before in the Bendheim, Flinn or GAS Galleries or accepted into a previous GAS juried exhibition. Wall works are limited to 36 inches wide by 60 inches high framed or unframed, wired and ready to hang. Entering makes you a member of the society through August 2027: $80 covers membership plus one or two pieces, $100 covers three. Over $2,000 in cash and other awards is presented at the closing reception. Accepted work is posted on 10 October 2026, drop-off is 17-18 October, and the exhibition runs 22 October to 19 November 2026 at the Bendheim Gallery in Greenwich. All work must be for sale, with 30 per cent of each sale divided between GAS and the Bendheim Gallery. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: $80 membership (1-2 works), $100 (3 works). Prize: $2,000+ in cash and other awards.

item.title: Alaska AIR Artist in Residence 2027–2028 · Bunnell Street Arts Center
item.description: Bunnell Street Arts Center, a multidisciplinary non-profit founded in 1991 in a historic Trading Post building in Homer, Alaska, runs Alaska AIR: juried, fully funded residencies of generally one month, scheduled across the Alaskan fall, winter and spring of 2027 and 2028. One to four are awarded annually, and each carries a $2,000 stipend for a month (pro-rated if shorter), round-trip travel to Homer up to $1,000 in value, a $250 materials stipend and a private bedroom with private bath in a shared apartment above the arts centre or nearby in the Old Town neighbourhood. The studio is Bunnell's 1,000 sq ft main exhibition gallery, open to the public during gallery hours, and the equipment list includes a darkroom (no enlarger), an HD video camera and tripod, an HD/3D projector, a nipping press and a small printing press. Bunnell accepts artists working in mediums "including (but not limited to) visual arts, literary arts, performing arts, social and civic practice, ephemeral art, moving image, movement and dance, music composition and performance", and looks for a clear, unified body of work alongside a specific proposal with a strong community engagement component — collective art-making, an Artist in Schools programme, a workshop, an exhibit, screening or reading. Residents generally give an introductory artist talk plus that community component. Open to international, US and Alaska artists; applications are accepted 1 September to 15 October and applicants are notified by 31 December. The $25 application fee can be waived on a needs basis by emailing the programme before applying. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: $25 (needs-based waivers available). Prize: Residency + $2,000 stipend, travel & materials.

item.title: Freezer Festival 2026 Open Call — Lo Real
item.description: The third edition of Argentina's Freezer festival takes Lo real — the real, or something real — as its theme, asking what survives of photography's claim on reality in a world saturated with digital simulation. The call selects one artist for a solo exhibition in La Plata, ten photographers whose single images are shown in venues across the city, and twenty photographic projects presented as one-to-five-minute audiovisual pieces. Selected work joins the official November 2026 programme across La Plata, Berisso, Ensenada and Buenos Aires alongside national and international artists, with production support for the solo show and promotion through the festival's press and platforms. This edition also forms part of the 8th Biennial of Art and Culture of the Universidad Nacional de La Plata, marking fifty years since the 1976 dictatorship, and the organisers explicitly invite work on archives, material memory and the histories that resist erasure. Open to photographers, visual artists and collectives of any nationality; submit up to fifteen photographs. Entry is a symbolic $12 USD or €10 by PayPal, waived for photography students and teachers at FDA UNLP and for retirees resident in Argentina. — Deadline: August 23, 2026. Fee: $12 / €10 (free for UNLP photography students and staff). Prize: Solo exhibition + citywide group exhibition.

item.title: The Power of the ARTS — 8th Annual Juried Exhibition · Marion Cultural Alliance
item.description: Marion Cultural Alliance marks twenty-five years of championing artists in Marion County with a juried exhibition about the arts themselves — a favourite discipline, a memorable performance, a beloved book, an inspiring mentor. Artists of all levels working in all media are invited, photography included, and interpretations may be realistic or abstract, traditional or contemporary. The show hangs at the Brick City Center for the Arts from 2 to 31 October 2026, opening with a reception on 2 October where the juror's awards are presented: $250 Best of Show, $150 first, $100 second, $50 third and two honorable mentions, alongside an MCA 25th Anniversary Award, a LILAC Foundation Purchase Award, executive staff recognitions and a Community Choice Award decided by public ribbon voting. Up to two original works per artist, suggested maximum forty inches in any direction, gallery-ready; no prints, reproductions or work previously shown at the Brick. All accepted work must be for sale, split 70 percent to the artist and 30 percent to MCA. An active MCA artist membership is required to participate, from $35 a year, and work is dropped off and collected in person in Ocala. — Deadline: September 21, 2026. Fee: $15 (1 entry) / $25 (2 entries). Prize: $250 Best of Show + cash awards.

item.title: Candace Freeland Photography of Merit Award 2026 · The Mitford Museum
item.description: A free, cash-funded photography award for young photographers, founded by the photojournalist Candace Freeland (1952-2021) — an Associated Press, Charlotte Observer, New York Times and Washington Post contributor whose exhibitions included Forced Out: The Agony of the Refugee in Our Time for Amnesty International — and now run by The Mitford Museum in Hudson, North Carolina, the museum founded by her mother, the novelist Jan Karon. US residents aged 8 to 22 are invited to submit photographs made on a cell phone on the theme Food and Family. There are two categories, colour and black and white, judged in two age groups, 8-15 and 16-22; you may enter one photograph in each category provided the two images are markedly different, and entering both still leaves you eligible for only one juried award. Files must be high resolution and able to resize to an 11 by 14 inch print. The jurors are Maggie Flanigan, director of the AFA Visual Arts programme at Caldwell Community College, whose own lens-based work looks at religion and community in the rural South; Tim Barnwell, an Asheville photographer with work in the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Asheville Art Museum; and Tom Rankin, who heads Duke University's MFA in Experimental and Documentary Arts. Each of the four category-and-age-group slots carries a $500 Grand Prize, a $250 Runner-Up and a $250 People's Choice voted by the public, and the museum runs free smartphone photography workshops in the run-up. Winners are announced at a reception on 9 October 2026. Note that the museum's two surfaces disagree: its Merit Awards page gives a 1 November deadline and a $750 top prize for the 16-22 group, while the official rules attached to the entry form give 1 September, $500 across all four slots, and the October reception. The form is the document entrants agree to, so enter by 1 September. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $4,000 in cash awards.

item.title: Midwest Regional 2027 · Artlink Contemporary Gallery
item.description: Artlink's annual juried group exhibition for artists living in the American Midwest, open to any medium and any size and shown across the gallery's main space. Artlink is a nonprofit contemporary gallery in the Auer Center for Arts & Culture in downtown Fort Wayne, running since 1978 and funded in part by Arts United and the Indiana Arts Commission. Eligible states are Indiana, Ohio, Michigan, Illinois, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Iowa, Missouri, North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska and Kansas; entrants must be 18 or over, and work must have been made in the last five years and not shown at Artlink before. Reproductions are not accepted. Entry is $12 per work with a limit of ten entries, and the juror gives three cash awards for first, second and third place — Artlink does not publish the amounts. Accepted work must arrive ready to install, framed pieces included, and anything damaged or differing from what was accepted may be turned away. A 35% sales fee applies to work sold, with artists paid by cheque after the show closes; work is insured while at the gallery but not in transit. The exhibition runs 7 January to 7 February 2027, opening with a reception on 7 January from 5 to 8pm. — Deadline: November 9, 2026. Fee: $12 per entry. Prize: 3 cash awards + exhibition.

item.title: Where I Sleep · Forum 301
item.description: Forum 301 is a gallery and discussion space at 301 W. Ohio Street in Chicago's River North, built around open-ended forums that use exhibitions as a starting point for conversation between artists, scholars and students. For its September exhibition the gallery is seeking artists experimenting in the photographic medium. Where I Sleep presents artists who investigate the nuances of “home” through various photographic practices, each examining the complexities of connecting to a physical space, with the works drawing viewers to consider the isolated opportunities seated inside an individual's sense of home, including the potential to encourage memory, seeing and story. Accepted works include photographic prints, and the gallery explicitly encourages artists to think beyond a photo on a wall, whether that means projections, sculptural work, work in book form or something else. Four submissions are allowed for a single $20 fee, and applications are made through a form on the gallery's own site that asks for an artist statement or bio plus materials, dimensions and year for each work. Applications close August 23, 2026 and the exhibition runs September 4 to October 4, 2026. — Deadline: August 23, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Anemone Vol. 1, No. 2
item.description: Anemone is a print magazine published out of Bozeman, Montana by pulphead, a community writing and coffee space, and is built around what it calls the analog perspective: a framing rooted in continuity, tangibility, lived experience, slowness, emphasis on process and “grace for imperfection”, set against one of replicability, speed, binary outcomes and optimization. Its first issue came out in July 2026 and submissions are now open for Vol. 1, No. 2. Photography and visual art sit alongside short fiction, creative nonfiction, reportage and poetry as full submission categories, and the theme is stated broadly as the world as told by Montanans; all styles and all subjects are welcome, with the subject asked to evoke the themes, pitfalls, joys and moments of the day as best one reasonably can. Photographs must be unpublished, though exceptions are made for work self-published to an online portfolio or personal socials, and files are uploaded through a form on the magazine's own site as JPEG, JPG or PNG at 150 to 300 dpi and under 20 MB, accompanied by a single written document captioning each image with date, location, title, medium and inspiration. There is no submission fee. The magazine is emphatic about generative tools: “use AI to originate work and you will be choked out with a Full Nelson, then disqualified.” Contributors are paid — the guidelines state that no work will be published without net-ninety payment arranged from the date of publishing, at negotiated per-word or per-placement rates — and unselected work is held in a slushpile for possible use in a later edition. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication + payment.

item.title: Community Art Gallery — Fall 2026 Show · City of San Marcos
item.description: The City of San Marcos established its Community Art Gallery in 2024 in the lobby of City Hall, as a space to share art with residents and visitors and to elevate the arts in the community. For the Fall 2026 show the city is accepting work from artists aged 18 and over living in Hays, Caldwell, Comal and Guadalupe Counties in central Texas. All two-dimensional and three-dimensional media that can be safely hung on the walls are eligible, so photography qualifies; the only content restrictions are that work for this family-friendly public venue must be apolitical, non-violent and G-rated, with no nudity even if tasteful and artistic. Applicants submit an artist bio and up to three artworks available for loan for the duration of the exhibition, sized between 8 by 10 inches and 24 by 36 inches and weighing no more than 30 pounds, arriving ready to hang with hardware installed. A three-member jury makes the selection and space is limited, so inclusion is not guaranteed. There is no entry fee. Work may be offered for sale or marked not for sale, the gallery retains no commission, and any sale is conducted directly between artist and buyer. The submission window runs August 12 to 31, applications are reviewed September 1 to 9, artists are notified September 10, art intake is Saturday October 3 from 10am to 1.30pm, and the exhibit hangs from October 2026 through March 2027. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Small Works 2026 · Winterville Cultural Center Gallery
item.description: The Winterville Cultural Center Gallery, in the renovated 1950s high school just outside Athens, Georgia, invites artists across the United States to submit small-scale work for its National Juried Small Works Exhibition 2026. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, ceramics, sculpture, fiber and mixed media; no reproductions or giclees, and AI-generated artwork is not eligible. Work may not exceed 14 inches in any direction including the frame, and three-dimensional work may not exceed 14 inches in height, width or depth. Yu-Kai Lin, founder and director of Kai Lin Art in Atlanta, selects the exhibition and all three awards: Best in Show $500, Juror's Award $250 and a People's Choice Award of $100, $850 in cash in total. Up to three works may be entered for a single fee. Acceptances are sent September 12, shipped work is due September 23 and hand delivery runs September 24 to 26; the show opens to the public on October 7 with a reception on October 9 and closes December 15, 2026. All accepted work must be for sale for the run of the exhibition, with 65 percent of any sale to the artist and 35 percent to the gallery, and artists cover shipping both ways. Two-dimensional work must arrive framed and wired, with no sawtooth hangers. Entries are JPEG only, cropped to the artwork edges, 2 MB maximum. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: $35 ($25 members). Prize: $850 in cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Indian Photo Festival Open Call 2026
item.description: The Indian Photo Festival invites photographers, visual storytellers, artists, curators, collectives, archives, galleries and organisations worldwide to submit work for the exhibitions of its 12th edition, held in Hyderabad from 26 November 2026 to 3 January 2027. The theme is open: the festival welcomes cohesive bodies of work from all genres of photography and lens-based storytelling, including documentary, conceptual, fine art, portraiture, landscape, street, experimental practices, archival projects and mixed media, and states that submissions are judged on artistic merit, originality, coherence, visual quality, storytelling and conceptual strength rather than genre. Alongside the exhibition call, the festival is also inviting published, self-published, independently produced and dummy photobooks, as well as zines, for the Indian Photo Festival Photobook Exhibition; photobooks are submitted as a single PDF of all pages and spreads, and selected titles are invited to send one physical copy for display. Selected exhibition projects are professionally produced and exhibited by the festival at no cost to the participant, which bears the production costs of exhibition prints and display materials. There is no entry fee. Submissions require a minimum of 15 and a maximum of 30 images, plus an artist statement and biography of up to 500 words each. Only shortlisted applicants are contacted. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Gift of Art 2026 · Hal Bromm Gallery
item.description: Hal Bromm established Tribeca's first contemporary gallery in 1975, showing early minimal and conceptual work by Carl Andre, Rosemarie Castoro, Victor Burgin and John Hilliard, and giving early solo exhibitions to Krzysztof Wodiczko, Keith Haring and David Wojnarowicz. The gallery shows photography as a matter of course: its summer 2026 exhibition photo·graph surveyed contemporary photographic practice with work by Bernd and Hilla Becher, Renate Aller, Slava Mogutin and others. Since the 1980s THE GIFT OF ART has been the gallery's annual holiday tradition, in which artists are invited to make unique, saleable artworks as ornaments to adorn the gallery tree - often with overtly political themes that challenged the usual sugar plums and Christmas angels. Last year's edition featured over 100 handmade ornaments by more than 60 artists from around the globe. For 2026 the gallery is expanding the show to include artist-made prints, so the work can live in a home year-round. Each artist may submit up to three ornaments and two prints, and may enter one or both categories. Submissions are reviewed on a rolling basis and artists are notified no later than 10 October 2026. Both ornaments and prints are for sale at the gallery throughout December, with 30% of proceeds going to Rehabilitation Through the Arts, which has run arts programming in New York prisons since 1996. The exhibition runs 1 to 19 December 2026. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: searching for beauty · A Smith Gallery
item.description: A Smith Gallery in Johnson City, Texas announces "searching for beauty", the next in its long-running series of juried online photography exhibitions. The juror is Wendi Schneider. Selected work is shown in the gallery's online exhibition from 16 October to 26 November 2026, with a reception on 31 October 2026 at 3pm CST and a GalleryTalk video posted in ASG Conversations. A Smith runs these calls on a rolling calendar and typically selects several dozen images for the online gallery and an accompanying exhibition catalogue; its calls are open to professional and amateur photographers worldwide working in all photographic mediums, and work previously exhibited in an A Smith Gallery competition is not eligible. The full prospectus, including the entry fee and image limits, had not yet been published at the time of listing - check the gallery's Calls for Entry page for the entry form once the call opens. — Deadline: September 21, 2026. Fee: See website. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: animalia · A Smith Gallery
item.description: A Smith Gallery in Johnson City, Texas announces "animalia", a juried online photography exhibition on animals, juried by Traer Scott. Selected work is shown in the gallery's online exhibition from 27 November 2026 to 7 January 2027, with a reception on 26 December 2026 at 3pm CST and a GalleryTalk video posted in ASG Conversations. A Smith runs these calls on a rolling calendar and typically selects several dozen images for the online gallery and an accompanying exhibition catalogue; its calls are open to professional and amateur photographers worldwide working in all photographic mediums, and work previously exhibited in an A Smith Gallery competition is not eligible. The full prospectus, including the entry fee and image limits, had not yet been published at the time of listing - check the gallery's Calls for Entry page for the entry form once the call opens. — Deadline: November 2, 2026. Fee: See website. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Exhibition Open Call · PS122 Gallery
item.description: PS122 Gallery, the not-for-profit alternative exhibition space that has run out of the city-owned 122 Community Center in New York's East Village since 1979, invites proposals for its 2027 season. A three-person jury of arts professionals will select six curator- and/or artist-led exhibitions, each running for a month in the gallery's roughly 1,000 square foot space, with exhibitions scheduled across February, March, April, June, September and October 2027. Proposals must involve at least two artists working in any medium, and either the curator or the artists must live in one of the five New York City boroughs; collectives are encouraged, as are experimental uses of the space, in which case public programmes with an aesthetic component are welcomed but not required. Currently enrolled students are not eligible and each applicant is limited to one submission. The application is free and asks for a 500-word exhibition proposal, the names of the confirmed participating artists, a combined PDF of up to ten images of work, installation shots or a proposed layout with captions, and a combined PDF of CVs for everyone involved. Held annually since the 1986-87 season and restarted in 2023, the open call helped define the gallery's history: it gave early exhibitions to Peter Halley, Keith Haring and Amy Sillman, and the programme has shown Nan Goldin, Barbara Kruger, Louise Bourgeois, Glenn Ligon, Alfredo Jaar, Kiki Smith and David Wojnarowicz among hundreds of others. The gallery is a programme of Painting Space 122 Inc, an artist-run cooperative, and is supported in part by public funds from the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs. Applicants are notified in October 2026. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Forum Box Open Call 2028
item.description: Forum Box is an artist-run cooperative gallery on the Helsinki waterfront with roughly 300 square metres of exhibition space, and it is now taking proposals for its 2028 programme. Artists, curators and working groups may apply for the whole space or for one or two of its three rooms — Permanto (about 65 m², three continuous walls, 5.6 m ceiling), Monttu (about 70 m², divided by stairs) and Parvi (about 90 m², 4.2 m ceiling and the most wall space). The standard slot is five weeks including installation, and for 2028 shorter project-based exhibitions and performances can also be proposed. Selection is made by an exhibition working group of member artists together with the executive director, and every selected artist is offered a member of Forum Box as a peer contact through the process. Applying is free: a single PDF of no more than 4MB containing the gallery's application form, an exhibition or project plan of up to two A4 pages, CVs and around ten images of recent work, emailed by 1pm Finnish time on 7 September 2026. Exhibiting artists currently pay a space rent — €280 for four weeks in the whole gallery or €100 for one room, dropping to €125 and €70 for a single week — which covers communication, marketing, invigilation and sales handling, and the cooperative states it aims to be entirely rent-free by 2028 and has reduced rents every year since 2020; a 40% commission (plus VAT) applies to work sold. Two conditions are worth reading before applying: solo exhibitions carry a five-year minimum interval between shows at Forum Box, and artists may not hold a solo exhibition elsewhere in the Helsinki metropolitan area in the twelve months before their own. A separate, rent-free strand in the same application window seeks a proposal for the Lux Galleries programme of the Lux Helsinki light art festival, on view 30 December 2027 to 9 January 2028, for which the five-year interval does not apply. All applicants hear by the end of October 2026. — Deadline: September 7, 2026. Fee: Free (€70–€280 space rent if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Fool's World Vol. 2.2
item.description: The Fool's World is a small travel literary magazine of poetry, prose and visual art, launched by the team behind Raleigh Review, and its summer reading window closes on 1 September. The visual art category is open to photographers in two forms: up to five individual works submitted as separate files, or a single PDF photo essay or series of up to twelve images, sequenced in the order it should be published and unified in theme or style, with a short statement. The editors read travel broadly — 'a deliciously ambiguous term', in their words — and say the work may be inspired by travel, depict travel itself, or simply reflect movement, as long as the experience is the photographer's own. Only previously unpublished work is considered and AI-generated submissions are banned outright. Submissions are free through the magazine's Duosuma portal, and the team aims to respond within four to six weeks. Physical works should be photographed cleanly, without glare or visible canvas edges unless that is an intentional choice, and accepted work may be asked to be rephotographed to meet print standards. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Fragments of the Everyday · Exposure Photo Gallery
item.description: Exposure Photo Gallery's third open call invites photographers to submit images that find meaning in the world around us — places, people, gestures, scenes and moments, from the extraordinary to the seemingly ordinary. There is no single way to interpret the everyday: it can be found on a street or in a remote landscape, in a face, a piece of architecture, an object, a spontaneous scene or a deliberate composition; what matters is the photographer's perspective. The juror is Steve McCurry, the American photographer whose Afghan Girl is among the most recognisable photographs in the world and who has spent more than five decades portraying cultures, people and scenes of everyday life. Selected work is shown in a group exhibition at the gallery in Río Tercero, Córdoba: a Gold, a Silver and a Bronze Award, ten Honorable Mentions whose prints hang in the physical show, thirty-seven Juror's Selections shown digitally, and special recognitions reserved for photographers from Córdoba Province. The Gold Award winner also takes US$500 and a solo exhibition at the gallery, on a date arranged with the artist. Selected and winning works appear in a print-on-demand exhibition book, and an Online Gallery Special Recognition marks roughly the top 7.5 per cent of entries. All awards are issued as digital diplomas. Fees are tiered by image count and there is no cap on how many photographs may be submitted. Entries close 31 March 2027 at 11:59 PM Pacific time; winners are announced 3 May 2027 and hi-res files are due 14 May. — Deadline: March 31, 2027. Fee: $10–$30. Prize: $500 + solo exhibition (Gold Award).

item.title: Kirloskar Art Grant 2026 · S. L. Kirloskar CSR Foundation
item.description: The second edition of the S. L. Kirloskar CSR Foundation's annual grant for lens-based practitioners, supporting artists whose work interrogates contemporary relationships between people, environments and systems in an age of globalisation, digital saturation and cultural transformation. The Foundation frames photography and moving image not only as tools of representation but as instruments for questioning dominant narratives and creating new ones, and invites proposals engaging critically with sustainability and environment, science and innovation, biodiversity and nature, culture and heritage, or community and social change. Two recipients — one photographer and one moving-image artist — are selected by a jury, each receiving a production grant of INR 5 lakh, of which up to 35 per cent may be taken as an artist fee or honorarium, plus opportunities to show the completed project at Kirloskar Group premises and other venues across India. Applications are open to emerging practitioners working in documentary, conceptual, experimental or new media formats who reside in India and hold Indian citizenship; individuals and artist duos or collectives may apply. Submissions go by email and comprise a project proposal of up to 1,000 words, a 500-word artist statement, a portfolio of five to ten captioned images or videos as a PDF under 5 MB, a CV, a budget breakdown and a project timeline. Equipment purchases are not covered, though project-related consumables such as film, cards, ink and paper are. The project period runs 21 September 2026 to 21 March 2027, and copyright remains with the artist. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: INR 5 lakh cash grant each (2 awards).

item.title: Photographic Nights of Selma 2026
item.description: The seventh edition of a festival founded by French photographer Stéphane Kossmann — who also founded Les Nuits Photographiques de Pierrevert — in partnership with Foot Soldier Park and Arts Revive in Selma, Alabama. Around thirty selected artist projects are shown each evening on a giant outdoor screen, with daytime given over to exhibitions across the Selma area, encounters between photographers and the public, portfolio readings and conferences. There is no set theme: the artistic committee asks only for a unique perspective and a clearly asserted point of view in a series of fifteen to thirty photographs, and is looking for a broad panorama of recent work of all kinds — reflections on society, landscape, fashion, portraiture, still life, explorations of intimacy, or proposals diverging from the current zeitgeist. Selected series are presented as photo-sound montages of no more than four minutes; the festival's video and sound editors can build the montage, or photographers may submit their own edit, and an original soundtrack may be supplied. Each selected photographer commits to attending the evening of their screening and the following day; photographers stay in local homes for the duration, limited to fifteen places, with lunches covered by the festival and travel at the photographer's own expense. Prizes are awarded at the end by a jury of figures from photography and the arts and by the public, and the Jury Prize carries an invitation with travel expenses covered to the Nuits Photographiques de Pierrevert in the south of France in the last week of July 2027. Applicants must declare any use of image-generation tools. The festival runs 6–7 November 2026 and access to exhibitions, screenings and conferences is free. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Santu Mofokeng Foundation Photography Prize 2026
item.description: A new national award from the Santu Mofokeng Foundation, established in honour of one of South Africa's most influential photographers and dedicated to recognising and supporting outstanding emerging photographers working in the country. Through a national open call the Foundation seeks artists whose work shows a thoughtful and compelling engagement with the photographic medium, reflecting the depth, sensitivity and critical awareness that characterised Mofokeng's own practice, and aims to provide recognition, visibility and professional support at a pivotal stage in a career. The inaugural award carries a R100,000 cash prize together with editorial support, an artist profile and opportunities for future exhibition presentation through the programmes of Latitudes, the Foundation's promotional and platform partner. Entry is open to independent practitioners living and working in South Africa; the application form sets an age ceiling of 45 and asks for a cohesive body of ten to fifteen photographs made within the past five years, alongside a portrait image, a recent biography and statements describing the applicant's practice, the submitted body of work and why they would be a strong recipient. The Foundation was established in 2015, when Mofokeng donated his photographic work and copyright to it, and works to preserve, research and share his legacy while supporting contemporary photographic practice through exhibitions, publications and public programmes. Applications close on 15 October 2026. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: R100,000.

item.title: Helpmann Fellowships 2026 · Helpmann Academy
item.description: Three fellowships of up to A$7,500 for emerging South Australian creatives, funded by the James & Diana Ramsay Foundation. The fellowships are self-determined: applicants propose their own bold, ambitious project, which may be the creation of new work, an exhibition, a residency or internship, touring, specialised training, a longer professional development programme, or a combination. Photography is one of nineteen disciplines on the application form, alongside painting, sculpture, moving image, printmaking, new media and curatorial practice. Applicants must be final-year students or graduates within five years of a supported degree at Adelaide University, Flinders University, the University of Adelaide or the University of South Australia, and must currently reside in South Australia; master's and PhD candidates qualify only through their undergraduate or honours study. Applications are assessed on artistic merit, alignment with career development, feasibility, commitment to learning and level of ambition, and require an artist CV, academic transcript, budget on the Academy's template, timeline, project confirmations, two letters of support and four to six images or one to two audio-visual demos. Funded activity must take place between 1 January and 31 December 2027. There is no application fee. Outcomes are notified within four weeks of the closing date and fellowships are presented at a private event in October. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: A$7,500 × 3.

item.title: 8th Annual Art + Stroll
item.description: A juried exhibition of original 2D and 3D fine art in all mediums and styles, staged across downtown Fort Lauderdale by Business for the Arts of Broward. Selected work hangs for a week in the lobbies of 200 and 201 East Las Olas Boulevard — joined this year by Huizenga Park — before the signature Art + Stroll evening on Thursday 12 November 2026, when the Las Olas business district fills with juried visual art, live performances, interactive demonstrations and cultural programming. Selected work is also shown digitally on the BFA Broward website, and each accepted artist receives a complimentary Sip + Stroll VIP ticket. Over $5,000 in cash awards is on offer: $3,000 Best in Show, $1,500 second, $500 third and a $300 Judge's Recognition. The $30 fee covers up to three works; pieces may not exceed 36 inches in their longest dimension or 30 pounds, must arrive exhibition-ready and wired with D-rings, and all work may be offered for sale with BFA retaining 25 per cent commission. Open to artists 18 and over. Note that the CaFE application portal does not open until 17 August 2026. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: $5,300 across four awards.

item.title: Pet Project
item.description: The Bedford's annual juried exhibition returns with Pet Project, a whimsical spin through the joy of the animal companions who captivate us with their larger-than-life personalities and quirks — a playful menagerie of muses and mischief-makers who slither, flutter, scamper and pounce their way into our lives. The call is open to all media and to US-based artists 18 and over; only artwork about pets will be juried. Artists may submit up to three works, with no size limit in principle though the gallery reserves the right to decline exceptionally large or cumbersome pieces, and 2D work must arrive framed where applicable and ready to hang. Jurors are to be announced, and $2,000 in cash prizes will be given as juror awards. The $40 entry fee is waived for anyone who donates $50 or more to the Bedford before applying, using a donor code entered at checkout. Notice of participation goes out 23 April 2027, work is delivered 14–18 June and the exhibition runs 10 July to 12 September 2027 at the Bedford Gallery in the Lesher Center for the Arts, opening with a party on 10 July. Artists are encouraged but not required to list work for sale; the gallery's commission structure is 60 per cent of the sale price to the artist and 40 per cent retained. — Deadline: March 24, 2027. Fee: $40 (free for Bedford donors of $50+). Prize: $2,000 in juror awards.

item.title: Josephine Ulrick and Win Schubert Photography Award 2026 · HOTA, Home of the Arts
item.description: Queensland's richest acquisitive photographic prize returns to HOTA Gallery on the Gold Coast: A$25,000 and acquisition into the HOTA Collection for the winner, plus a A$5,000 People's Choice Award decided by public vote. Submissions are invited across the traditional and expanded medium, including photocollage, sculpture, projection, installation and cameraless photography. Finalists are chosen by a panel of 2018 award winner Tamara Dean, UNSW Galleries director José Da Silva and independent writer and curator Mikala Tai, and are shown in the award exhibition at HOTA Gallery from 28 November 2026 to 7 March 2027. Previous winners include Polly Borland, Merilyn Fairskye, Shaun Gladwell, Polixeni Papapetrou, Darren Sylvester and Justine Varga. Entrants must be 18 or over and Australian citizens or permanent residents; individuals and groups may enter, but nobody may appear in more than one submission. Entry is limited to one artwork, created on or after 11 May 2025 and no larger than 300 cm in any dimension including frame or mount, and work must be available for the full exhibition period. AI may be used provided the extent of that use is clearly described in the submission. The entry fee has been reduced to A$15, with A$10 Mob Tix for First Nations applicants. Finalists are notified by email or phone and have seven days to accept; the winner is announced at the exhibition opening. — Deadline: August 17, 2026. Fee: A$15 (A$10 Mob Tix). Prize: A$25,000 acquisitive + A$5,000 People's Choice.

item.title: MYPH Photography Prize 2026 · MYPH
item.description: The third annual, free prize from the MYPH school of conceptual and art photography, open to Ukrainian citizens living in Ukraine or abroad who have no more than five years of active practice with the photographic medium — which MYPH defines as conscious, regular, consistent work in art photography, from making one's own projects and series to exhibitions, competitions, residencies, portfolio reviews, publication and engagement with the artistic community. Fine art, conceptual and documentary photography are all invited, and every photographic technique and form of visual manipulation is accepted, from analogue shooting to digital collage and experiment. Applicants submit a series or project of eight to ten photographs made in 2025 or 2026; ongoing projects are welcome, and last year's winners may enter with new work. The Grand Prix takes a Fujifilm X-series camera and lens, a 50,000 UAH MYPH tuition certificate, membership of the Ukrainian Association of Professional Photographers, and showings at Art Market Budapest and Art Kyiv Fair; second and third places take MYPH tuition certificates of 25,000 and 10,000 UAH rather than prize money, and a separate Fujifilm 'Best Debut' prize goes to an author showing a series publicly for the first time. Eight finalists exhibit together at Dymchuk Gallery in Kyiv, with the show travelling in Ukraine and abroad as part of MYPH Photo Festival, and partner prizes include a 15,000 UAH cash award for one woman photographer, print production, photobooks and further tuition certificates. Applicants must be 18 at the time of applying. Finalists are announced on 13 October 2026 and the winners at the exhibition ceremony on 23 October. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Fujifilm camera + 50,000 UAH tuition.

item.title: Exposure 2027 International Open Call
item.description: The Exposure Photography Festival is a month-long celebration of photography that takes over Alberta every February. Its International Open Call is for photographers and visual artists anywhere in the world, at any stage of their career, who incorporate, celebrate or challenge the photographic medium. There is no set theme and no preferred style: images can be shot in any format with any camera and may include collage or experimental approaches. Jurors are given an open mandate and weigh artistic strength, contemporary relevance and resonance, how the work would read in a public exhibition, and curatorial breadth across practices, subject matter, geographic and cultural contexts and career stages. Selected artists show in a group exhibition at TRUCK Contemporary Art in Mohkinstis (Calgary) for the whole of February 2027, free and open to the public, and receive a CA$456 artist fee calculated according to CARFAC guidelines, a CA$50 production expense allocation and a 20 per cent discount with print partner ABL Imaging to prepare the work; mounting and framing decisions are made collaboratively with Exposure's curatorial team. Selected images from every exhibiting artist also appear in a public billboard exhibition on Pattison Outdoor digital screens around Calgary, and each artist gets a profile on Exposure's website alongside social and press promotion. Submit at least five images from a strong, connected series with a short statement; the fee covers up to five images, with further images CA$5 each up to ten in total. Ten fee waivers are available to artists facing economic hardship, decided first come first served with a reply inside 48 hours, and photographers based in non-high-income countries can apply free through a separate form. The 2027 jury will be one international juror, one Exposure board member and the festival manager, to be announced. Notification October 31, 2026; prints due December 2026. — Deadline: October 5, 2026. Fee: CA$45 (+CA$5 per extra image). Prize: CA$456 artist fee + Exhibition.
